O vaivém do terminal: The back and forth of the terminal
Você escreve, ele responde, e o > volta: You type, it answers, and the > comes back, waiting for you.
Ao abrir, o cmd mostra uma linha curta q: When it opens, cmd shows a short line that ends in >, with a blinking cursor. That's the computer waiting for you. Nothing happens until you type and press Enter.
Leia o caminho como endereço. Cada barra: Read the path like an address. Each backslash separates a folder, and the last one is where you are right now. Your personal folder is C:\Users\ followed by your username.
A linha sem <code>&gt;</code> é a respos: The line without > is the computer's answer. Many commands that work give no answer at all: the next command confirms it, like cd or dir.
O terminal e o Explorador mostram o mesm: The terminal and File Explorer show the same disk. Create a folder in one, and it shows up in the other. The explorer . command opens the file window right in the folder you're in.
Comando, resposta e o > de volta: é semp: Command, answer, and the > back again: it's always this back and forth
No Mac e no Linux o terminal se chama Te: On Mac and Linux the terminal is called Terminal and ends in $; the commands have different names (table at the end of the lesson).
Antes de qualquer comando que muda algo,: Before any command that changes something, look at the path before the >. Many errors that look like an AI failure are just the wrong folder: if you don't know where you are, the agent doesn't either.
